title: Chronic cranial window implantation for high-resolution intravital imaging of the endothelial glycocalyx in mouse cortex
protocol: Place the animal into the induction chamber with 4% isoflurane in oxygen or medical air.
Shave the surgical area.
Transition the animal to the stereotactic frame. Hook the teeth into the hole in the incisor bar and fix the ear bars in place.
Check head stability.
Maintain anesthesia at an isoflurane level of 2%–2.5% in oxygen or medical air, delivered continuously through a nose cone.
Monitor isoflurane level throughout the experiment to maintain depth of anesthesia.
Confirm depth of anesthesia with stable breathing and absence of a pedal reflex.
Use a homeothermic closed loop monitoring system to maintain the animal’s body temperature at 37.5 degrees throughout the experiment.
Cover the animal with cotton wool to maintain body temperature.
Give analgesics.
Subcutaneous injection of meloxicam 5 μg/g under the dorsal skin on the back.
Subcutaneous injection of bupivicaine/epinephrine 4 μg/g
Record time of drug administration.
Apply eye ointment.
Swab surgical area with iodine in a triangular shape from between the eyes to between the ears.
Apply liquid plaster on top of the iodine and allow to dry.
Remove a section of skin on top of the head.
Pinch the skin between the eyes with forceps and make an incision using scissors.
Insert scissors into opening and cut a triangular flap of skin to expose the scalp.
Make sure not to damage the lateral muscles.
Remove the periosteum using sterilized cotton buds, forceps and scissors to fully expose the bone.
Secure the wound margin with 3M Vetbond Tissue Adhesive.
Use a high-speed micro drill to lightly drill around the perimeter of the engraving.
Make the craniotomy region clear.
Mount the head plate using dental cement.
Drill the bone until sufficiently thin.
Secure a sterilized suture to the bone that will be removed using a small amount of dental cement.
Allow the dental cement to set with each end of the suture on either side.
Gently pull up the suture at both sides to remove the bone flap and expose the brain.
Secure the cranial window in place using 3M Vetbond Tissue Adhesive.
Use clear dental cement to further secure the cranial window.
Compose dental cement according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Position the large circular gap in the center of the head plate above the region where the craniotomy will be.
Hold the head plate in the correct orientation until the dental cement is dry.
Gently thin the bone around the craniotomy region using a high-speed micro drill set at approximately 14,000 rpm.
Move in a circular motion while drilling to avoid local heating of the tissue.
Remove bone debris using compressed air regularly to keep the area clear and visible for drilling.
Soak the area with saline intermittently to help prevent heat damage.
Serially assess the thickness of remaining bone.
Check that the drilled bone has been thinned sufficiently by pressing down very gently at the center of the circular piece of bone to be removed using forceps.
Use a drop of dental cement to secure a sterile suture to the circular piece of bone.
Allow the dental cement to dry while soaking the surrounding drilled bone with saline.
Very gently raise the bone flap away, holding the suture tightly at both sides.
Soak the exposed brain dura with saline following bone removal.
Place a cranial window above the craniotomy with the 3 mm window at the bottom while saline is still on top of the brain.
Lower the window gently using forceps so that the 3 mm window fills the 3 mm craniotomy and the 4 mm window sits on top.
Remove saline from bone to the margin of the cranial window using eye spears.
Place a drop of 3M Vetbond Tissue Adhesive close to the window but not over the opening.
Use eye spears to carefully surround the window whilst holding it firmly in place and ensure that the glue does not seep underneath the window.
Once this has partially dried, use a small amount of clear dental cement to further secure the window around the perimeter.
Hold the window in place for several minutes until sufficiently dried.
Inject the animal with 0.5 mL of saline subcutaneously to rehydrate.
Put the animal into the recovery cage with an appropriate post-surgical diet.
Monitor recovery until the animal is fit for return to housing.
Complete the relevant documentation according to local animal regulations.
Monitor animals regularly in accordance with guidelines set out in the local animal regulations.
Keep track of bodyweight and condition.
Turn on the multiphoton laser at the control unit.
Allow the laser to reach full operating power.
Power on the rest of the multiphoton confocal system.
Launch the Leica LAS X confocal software.
Ensure that the XY stage initializes in the software.
Under the ‘configuration’ tab, select the ‘laser config’ option.
Switch on the required imaging lasers.
Place the animal into the induction chamber with 4% isoflurane in oxygen or medical air.
Continue anesthetic delivery through a nose cone to maintain anesthesia.
Fix the animal securely in place using the implanted head plate.
Maintain anesthesia at 1%–2% isoflurane in oxygen or medical air throughout the experiment.
Confirm depth of anesthesia with stable breathing and absence of a pedal reflex.
Check on the animal regularly.
Use the homeothermic closed loop monitoring system to maintain body temperature at 37.5 degrees throughout the experiment.
Clean the window using distilled water or appropriate solution and an eye spear prior to imaging to remove any debris.
Move the imaging platform into position so that the window is directly below the objective at the correct height.
Place distilled water on top of the window for imaging.
Lower the water dipping objective into the water.
Mix 15 mM sterile HCl with human recombinant leptin.
Perform intravenous injection of fluorescent markers.
Inject 100 μL of Wheat Germ Agglutinin Alexa Fluor 488 conjugate at 1 mg/mL for visualizing the glycocalyx in green.
Inject 50 μL of 10 mg/mL Neutral 70,000 MW Texas red Dextran to visualize the bloodstream in red.
Ensure that no room light can get to the sample by using a laser-safe black box or material shroud over the imaging platform.

Configure imaging parameters within LAS X software for multiphoton excitation using the MaiTai (Spectra-Physics) MP laser tuned to 800 nm with emitted signals imaged simultaneously onto external ND-HyD’s through BP525/50 and BP624/40 filters.
Acquire regions with the MaiTai MP laser tuned to 880 nm and emitted signals imaged onto an additional ND-HyD through a BP440/20 filter.
Select several regions within the cranial window for the experiment.
Set up the microscope to acquire high-resolution Z stacks of each selected region in sequence.
Acquire Z stacks with a depth of up to 200 μm and a Z step size of 2 μm.
Acquire baseline images of all ROIs.
Repeat imaging of these regions over the required time period for the experiment in the same or subsequent experiments.
